3745: def _collection_rows_by_folder(
3746:     session: Session,
3747:     owner_traveler_id: str,
3748: ) -> dict[str, list[tuple[CollectionItem, Place]]]:
3749:     """Every shelf row on every shelf one traveller owns, grouped by shelf, in two reads or fewer.
3750: 
3751:     The join is against `places` rather than a lookup per row, so listing ten shelves costs two
3752:     statements and not eleven.  It is an INNER join, and that is load-bearing rather than
3753:     incidental: `collection_items.place_id` references `places(id)` with no `ON DELETE` clause
3754:     (`backend/db/schema.sql`), and `PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON` is set on every connection
3755:     (`backend/app/db/session.py`), so a place a shelf points at cannot be deleted underneath
3756:     it.  A shelf row therefore always has a place to resolve to, and the join cannot quietly drop
3757:     a row and leave `item_count` short of what was asked for.
3758: 
3759:     The `collection_folders` leg is here so a scoped read never pulls another traveller's rows into
3760:     memory to filter them out afterwards; it costs nothing on the statement count and it keeps
3761:     "whose shelf" one fact rather than two.
3762: 
3763:     The order is the shelf's own: first put on, first read.  Nothing downstream re-sorts it, so the
3764:     order the screen renders is the order the server chose.
3765:     """
3766: 
3767:     grouped: dict[str, list[tuple[CollectionItem, Place]]] = {}
3768:     for item, place in session.execute(
3769:         select(CollectionItem, Place)
3770:         .join(CollectionFolder, CollectionFolder.id == CollectionItem.folder_id)
3771:         .join(Place, Place.id == CollectionItem.place_id)
3772:         .where(CollectionFolder.owner_traveler_id == owner_traveler_id)
3773:         .order_by(CollectionItem.added_at, CollectionItem.id)
3774:     ).all():
